sections.heading: TRAI Guidelines for Bulk SMS India and the DLT Setup Behind Them

blocks.html: Under TRAI's commercial communication rules, every business sending bulk SMS registers on the telecom operators' DLT platform, which is why DLT SMS compliance is the first thing to settle. Three registrations make up the setup: your business entity, your sender ID (called a header) and each message template. A message that does not match an approved template is rejected before it reaches the handset.

items.title: Entity registration:
items.desc: your legal business details are registered once on the operator portals and linked to your sending account.

items.title: Sender ID registration:
items.desc: sender ID registration for bulk SMS India businesses need gives recipients a recognisable header instead of an unknown number.

items.title: Template approval:
items.desc: DLT template approval for bulk SMS means every message format, with its variables, is approved before it is used.

items.title: Link whitelisting:
items.desc: TRAI directed in August 2024 that traffic carrying URLs, APKs or OTT links that are not whitelisted be blocked, so register every link you plan to include.

blocks.alt: DLT registration steps for bulk SMS in India covering entity, sender ID and template approval

blocks.html: Because this is where most first campaigns stall, a DLT registered bulk SMS provider should guide the paperwork rather than hand you a blank form, and bulk SMS with DLT registration support should be part of onboarding, not an add-on. You can read the regulator's own material on TRAI's website and the official press release on URL whitelisting. sections.heading: SMS Marketing and Consent: Staying Within DPDP Act Principles

blocks.html: Compliance does not end at DLT. SMS marketing works best when recipients expect your message, and the DPDP Act reinforces that with principles of clear consent, purpose limitation and easy withdrawal. DPDP Act and bulk SMS marketing meet at one point: how you collect numbers and how easily people can opt out.

items.desc: tell people what they will receive when you collect their number.

items.title: Honour opt-outs:

items.title: Respect DND:
items.desc: keep promotional sends away from DND-registered numbers and outside permitted hours.

items.title: Keep lists clean:
items.desc: remove numbers that bounce or never engage, which also keeps your delivery reports meaningful.

blocks.html: For the official position on data protection, see MeitY's website. This is practical guidance rather than legal advice, so check your own obligations with a qualified professional.

items.q: Is bulk SMS legal in India?
items.a: Yes, when it follows TRAI's commercial communication rules. Senders register their entity, sender ID and message templates on the operators' DLT platform, promotional messages avoid DND-registered numbers and go out between 9 AM and 9 PM, and links in messages are whitelisted. Consent and clear opt-out routes also matter under the DPDP Act. Check your own obligations with a professional.

items.q: How to send bulk SMS in India?
items.a: Register your business on a DLT platform, then register your sender ID and message templates. Choose a bulk SMS provider, link your entity to the account, upload your contact list or connect through the API, pick an approved template, and schedule or send. Check the delivery report afterwards. A provider that guides the DLT setup shortens the first step considerably.

items.q: What is the difference between promotional and transactional SMS?
items.a: Promotional SMS carries offers and marketing, cannot be sent to DND-registered numbers and is limited to 9 AM to 9 PM. Transactional SMS carries critical alerts such as banking notifications and OTPs, and can reach DND-registered numbers at any time. Service messages, like order and delivery updates, sit between the two. Each needs its own approved template and the correct category.

items.q: Is DLT registration mandatory for bulk SMS?
items.a: Yes, it is mandatory for commercial SMS in India. Operators check every message against registered entities, sender IDs and templates, so messages without DLT registration are rejected and never reach the recipient. In short, if you are wondering whether you can send bulk SMS without DLT registration, you cannot. DLT applies to SMS only; WhatsApp follows Meta's own business verification and template review instead.

items.q: What is a good SMS delivery rate in India?
items.a: Rather than chase a fixed percentage, look at the pattern. Ask for reports that split delivered, failed and rejected messages with reasons. Most failures trace back to DND numbers, invalid or inactive numbers and template or header mismatches, all of which you can reduce with clean lists and approved templates. A provider that shows the evidence is more trustworthy than one that quotes a headline figure.

items.q: How much does bulk SMS cost in India?
items.a: Bulk SMS is priced in paise per message, and the rate depends on volume, message category and route. Larger packages lower the per-SMS rate, and promotional and transactional rates differ. Also check what the rate includes, such as DLT support, reports and API access, and whether credits expire. Share your monthly volume by category to get an accurate quote.

That depends on the provider and the plan, so ask before you buy. Some packages carry a validity period after which unused credits lapse, while others allow rollover. Get the validity terms in writing, compare them across providers, and match package size to your real monthly sending so little is left unused.
